title: Brain MRI Pipeline
subtitle: From a T1 scan to tissue maps and QC
description: An end-to-end Nipype pipeline with FSL FAST, K-means and ANTs Atropos segmentation, tissue volumes, bias-correction metrics and an interactive 3D brain.
longDescription: A research and learning pipeline for T1-weighted MRI: AC-PC alignment, MNI152 registration, skull stripping and N4 bias correction, followed by a choice of FSL FAST, K-means or ANTs Atropos. It compares segmentation agreement, reports tissue volumes and QC metrics, and produces a 3D view and HTML report per scan. Demo scans come from openly licensed OpenNeuro data.
mascotLines: The first K-means run cut every brain into three equal parts. The brains were fine; the histogram wasn't.
N4 lowered the CJV on all three demo scans. Numbers, not vibes.
imageCaptions: One demo scan after each step: original, AC-PC, registered, skull stripped, N4.
The same slices segmented three ways: K-means, FSL FAST and ANTs Atropos.
N4's estimated bias field, and the grey and white matter peaks pulling apart after it.
Tissue volumes of the three demo scans: grey matter lands near 45% every time.
features: AC-PC alignment, registration, skull stripping and N4 correction
Selectable FAST, K-means or Atropos segmentation
Tissue volumes, Dice agreement and before/after QC
Interactive 3D brain, turntable GIF and HTML reports
challenges: Comparing tissue segmentation methods on the same corrected scan
solutions: A focused Docker image containing the required tools
Shared N4-corrected inputs with selectable primary segmentation
results: Reproducible CPU pipeline with openly licensed demo scans
Per-scan tissue maps, quantitative QC and HTML reports
why: It comes from the brain MRI preprocessing I did at Infortrend for an Alzheimer's diagnosis project. The open version wires FSL, ANTs and an AC-PC detector into one nipype graph in a 2 GB Docker image, so learning the steps no longer begins with downloading all 4.1 GB of FSL.
gains: Lets students and researchers watch each preprocessing step instead of trusting a black box: every node writes its own folder, so any in-between image opens in FSLeyes or ITK-SNAP. It's a teaching tool, not a medical device, and the README says so out loud.

flow.label: One overview page for the run

lessons: The first comparison had K-means cut every brain into near-equal thirds. The pipeline did it: K-means clustered the equalised image, whose histogram is flat.
K-means sorts voxels by brightness alone and gave 5 to 7 points less grey matter than FAST, so FAST became the default in November 2026.
N4 bias correction lowered the grey/white CJV on every demo scan (sub-01: 0.64 to 0.56), so the step earns its place with numbers.
